timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only Claude CLI stream reviewed via manifest accounting; no semantic events were projected from this source.
Parent trajectory derived the spec through reference probes, wrote /tmp/spec/SPEC.md, launched the workflow, and reported background execution.
First formatter child read the same spec/source, collected help-width reference output, and was interrupted before producing formatter.mjs.
Second formatter child repeated the same spec/source read and help-output collection, then was interrupted before delivering formatter.mjs.
Initial py-int/repr implementation child probed int/repr behavior, wrote py helpers, and was interrupted during extended verification.
Schedule implementation child wrote job, scheduler, and index modules and verified interval round trips against the executable.
Py-core child wrote errors, unicode, and surrogateescape helpers and reported large byte-identical fuzz verification.
Entry child wrote /output/test3.mjs and verified syntax plus reference behavior expectations pending peer modules.
Parser-related retry child read the shared spec/source and existing files, then advanced option parsing verification before interruption/retry.
Py sys/builtins child wrote argv, IO, terminal-width, and print helpers and verified byte-oriented edge cases.
Later parser child reviewed existing parser/index/action/error files during retry/integration work before another restart.
Initial parser child probed exact option and help semantics, then was interrupted before completing the parser deliverable.
Final formatter child read spec/source, wrote formatter.mjs, ran 413 width-by-stream checks, and returned a successful report.
Third formatter attempt read spec/source and gathered help reference outputs before an interrupt restarted the same workflow key.
Argparse core child completed actions, errors, and types modules with focused unit and reference-message checks.
Parser child wrote parser.mjs and index.mjs, applied fixes, then was interrupted before full end-to-end closure.
Py-int/repr retry read existing helpers, built differential cases for digit and whitespace behavior, and continued verification.
Workflow journal records child starts/results, including repeated starts for the same formatter key and other restarted implementation keys.

parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM .mjs, manual argv parity, exact int/argparse/schedule behavior, zero external dependencies, and /output artifact delivery.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent derived a detailed spec, then launched workflow children for module groups, entry, harness, integration, convergence, audits, repair, and final gate.
parallel.implementation: Children produced py runtime, argparse, schedule, and entry modules; formatter work was restarted after interruptions before a successful formatter result.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Workflow-integrated artifact contained test3.mjs and module tree under lib/py, lib/argparse, and lib/schedule; official artifact validation succeeded.
parallel.verification: Parallel child reports included reference probes, formatter width sweeps, fuzz/differential checks, and official evaluation completed 70/70.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official correctness defect remained, but the agent process timed out with returncode 143 and the final response file was empty.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same prompt requirements and executable-observation constraint without delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept the full migration, probing, implementation, repair, and verification loop in one serial trajectory with workflows disabled.
serial.implementation: Built a layered implementation for python/runtime, argparse, schedule, and test3.mjs, then fixed whitespace and usage-format divergences.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a coherent final artifact tree and a final response explaining each layer and the verification caveat about prog-name normalization.
serial.verification: Ran curated differential tests to 240/240, fuzz to 1800/1800, spot checks from a different cwd, and official evaluation passed 70/70.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task obligation is visible at closure; process completed normally with returncode 0.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same hard requirements: ESM .mjs files, manual argv parity, exact output, zero external dependencies, and /output delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and recognized the same migration and verification requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-coverage difference caused an outcome gap; both implemented the required behavior and passed official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the task into child-owned module groups, harness, integration, convergence, audit, repair, and final gate phases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial solved in one local thread with workflows disabled and no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit multi-agent ownership and retries; serial kept ownership centralized, avoiding child retry coordination.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied a long shared contract with exact exports and file ownership to children, but formatter replacements restarted from the broad brief instead of inherited checkpoints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried the same interface knowledge locally and adjusted the implementation while retaining prior findings.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key context difference is retry-state transfer: parallel repeated formatter discovery, while serial preserved its own findings across edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced modular py, argparse, schedule, and entry artifacts via specialized children and a formatter child that eventually completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented an alternate but equivalent module layout and repaired mismatches such as prog-name wrapping and whitespace handling.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both paths converged to passing code; parallel achieved this through delegated modules, serial through iterative local edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel journaled child starts/results, including multiple formatter restarts and a final formatter result, but the parent process timed out before a final user response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local checks, received the results immediately in the same trajectory, and delivered a final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child result lifecycle overhead and timeout closure; serial had no child join boundary and closed normally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel artifact validation copied a coherent final tree containing test3.mjs and the lib/py, lib/argparse, and lib/schedule modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial artifact validation copied a coherent final tree containing test3.mjs and its lib/python, lib/argparse, and lib/schedule modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No final shared-state collision changed correctness; both final trees were accepted, though parallel wrote through many children.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel passed official evaluation 70/70; child reports also included width and fuzz checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial passed official evaluation 70/70 and explicitly reported curated and randomized differential verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Official acceptance was identical; serial left clearer local verification narration before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed a long workflow with repeated child starts and ended with returncode 143/timed_out true despite a passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed with returncode 0, remaining budget, and a normal final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred adverse budget/closure pressure from workflow retries; serial completed without timeout.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current status is not discordant: both parallel and serial passed 70 of 70 samples. The concrete difference is that parallel achieved the accepted artifact through a multi-child workflow with repeated uncheckpointed formatter retries and timed out before final narrative closure, while serial completed the same task locally and returned a normal final answer.
parallel_contributors: Multi-agent module split produced a passing artifact but incurred retry overhead and timeout/empty-final closure.
serial_contributors: Single-threaded local repair preserved findings across iterations and closed with curated and fuzz verification.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a lib/py runtime layout while serial used lib/python and a textwrap helper; both layouts satisfied the official evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process-only adverse pattern retained for the parallel run
